title: Seat a click-type torque wrench on a busbar lug bolt and torque it to the click
instruction: Pick up the torque wrench standing on its rest, seat its socket fully on the lug bolt, and torque the bolt with it. The wrench is already set to the bolt's torque. Then let go.
context: Electricians and panel builders torque lug and terminal bolts to the value marked on the device with a calibrated torque tool; the US electrical code (NEC 110.14(D)) has required one where a value is marked since 2017. The tool starts in the hand, not on the bolt: the socket must be seated square and fully over the hex before pulling, or the socket cams off and rounds the head while the joint stays loose. Click-wrench instructions say: pull steadily at the grip and stop the moment the wrench clicks. The wrench does not limit torque, it only signals it: pulling on through the click keeps tightening, past the joint's +10 % tolerance, and an over-torqued screw stretches or the lug cracks; pulling through scores 0, as does any bolt turn without the socket seated. Abilities tested: seat a socket on an 8 mm hex, then stop a steady pull on a one-shot signal from the tool. Done by: electricians (about 780,000 US) and electrical equipment assemblers (O*NET 47-2111.00, 51-2022.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). The joint: a copper flat bar 20 x 6 mm, 12 cm long, on two glass-polyester standoff insulators 2.4 cm tall, runs from x 21 to 33 at y 0. On it, a tinned-copper tube lug for 16 mm2 (about 6 AWG) cable with an M5 hole (palm 18 x 12 x 3 mm, barrel 8 mm across), its cable (black PVC, 8 mm over the insulation) leading off forward. The bolt: M5 x 0.8 x 16 mm hex, class 8.8 zinc-plated steel, ISO 4017 head (7.88 mm across flats, 3.5 mm high, chamfered crown), with an ISO 7089 flat washer, vertical at x 24, y 0, through the lug and bar into an M5 self-clinching nut in the bar; it is a free body on its thread, driven only through the hex. The lug and the panel label are marked 3 N*m (the label is not modelled). The bolt starts snug, at 1.5 N*m (README). The tool: an adjustable click-type torque wrench (chrome-vanadium steel, 1/4-inch square drive, 2-10 N*m range, ISO 6789 Type II class A, +/-6 %), 26 cm long, set to 3 N*m. Under its drive, an inline rotary torque transducer (26 x 26 mm, 4 cm tall), then an 8 mm 6-point socket (ISO 2725-1; opening 8.2 mm across flats, 0.16 mm clearance per flat, 0.8 mm 45-degree mouth chamfer, 12 mm OD, 25 mm long). Steel fit surfaces have friction 0.3; only the rubber grip is grippy. A second block (9.8 x 4 x 9.7 cm tall) stands under the handle's pull arc beside the joint, its top level with the seated grip's underside: it carries the grip whenever the wrench is on the bolt. The wrench STARTS OFF THE BOLT, standing socket-down on the bench at x 30, y 6, its handle toward the right arm (-y), the rubber grip resting on a 6.3 cm block; head, transducer and socket 450 g, handle 100 g on a pivot in the head 4.5 cm from the socket axis, held in line by a sprung detent; the grip's load mark 21.5 cm from the axis, so 3 N*m takes 14 N there. Seated on the bolt the wrench's centre plane is 10.6 cm above the table. Sim only (real trials score from the transducer): 100 % of the set torque at 4.9 deg past snug, 110 % at 5.9 deg, yield at 230 % (17.7 deg); the sim's torques are 1/7 of the real ones (the wrench clicks at 2 N at the grip).
scoring: Seated: at least 2.8 mm of the head's 3.5 mm inside the socket, socket axis within 8 deg of the bolt's and 1 mm of coaxial, held 5 control steps; measured from the two bodies' poses. Peak torque P, in % of the set torque: on a real rig, the transducer's peak-hold reading (100 % = 3 N*m); in the sim, from the bolt's tightest turn past snug (100 % at 4.9 deg, 110 % at 5.9 deg). Clicked: the detent broke over (handle bent 1.5 deg on its pivot) with the socket seated. Fail, latched for the trial (score 0): the bolt moved 1 deg or more while the socket was NOT seated (half-seated torquing, camming, dragging); P over 110 % (pulled on through the click; the bolt yields at 230 %); or the bolt turned back more than 3 deg from its tightest. Score: 1.0 for torqued in tolerance: seated click, P 90-110 % (2.7-3.3 N*m) and the bolt still within 1 deg of its tightest; else 0.25 if the bolt is at least 1.5 deg past snug (under-torqued); else 0.1 for seated but never turned; else 0. Halved unless both grippers are at least 10 cm outside the wrench's bounding box and the bolt and grip are still (under 0.05 deg and 0.3 mm per control step). 1.0 is success, held for 1 s. Real rig: angles from the transducer's angle channel, from the snug paint mark. Scored at the last step. Possible scores: 0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Back the bolt off (fit a new bolt if its peak went over 110 % or the head was rounded); run it down by hand, then to 1.5 N*m on the transducer, and paint-mark the head and lug; check the wrench is set to 3 N*m and stand it back on its bench rest, socket down, grip on the block, handle toward the right arm.
fidelity: Hex head and socket cavity are real convex-hull meshes: 0.16 mm/flat clearance, chamfered lead-ins, steel mu 0.3, grip 1.2; the socket drives the bolt only through this contact. Bolt: friction hinge whose torque rises with angle (M5 estimate), 1/7 of real torque for the soft arm; 30 g sim bolt for stability. Detent: sprung hinge, drive calibrated (backend x20, break-trace measured), break-over to a 6 deg stop, re-arm. Seating scored from body poses. Flush-ring selector; ratchet not modelled.
